item.title: Haaretz against Ben Gvir: Red Cross visits have not resumed
item.description: A procedure formulated by the Israel Prison Service imposing restrictions on visits by Red Cross representatives to meet with terrorists has angered the Association for Civil Rights in Israel and the Haaretz newspaper.

item.description: Motor scooter driver and rider attempt to flee inspection in Beit Hanina, but slip. Police arrest driver following chase.

item.description: X has suspended the account of Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree, which was used to disseminate the organization’s propaganda and claim responsibility for attacks and launches.

item.title: Families warn of mounting distress aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: After more than 250 days without docking, families of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln are raising alarm over severe burnout, harsh conditions and reported suicide attempts.

item.title: Ra’am chairman meets with former MK Segalovitz over possible joint political run
item.description: Ra’am chairman meets with former MK Segalovitz, and the two agreed to continue discussions on a joint run. Otzma Yehudit: 'A fire sale-with the backing of the Left.'

item.title: Rome: Jewish tourist attacked twice in 24 hours
item.description: Yitzhak Dahan from Paris, who was visiting Rome on a family vacation, was pepper-sprayed near the Jewish Ghetto and, less than 24 hours later, was attacked by four unidentified individuals.

item.title: Binyamin governor denounces Qusra outpost
item.description: Yisrael Ganz, Governor of the Binyamin Regional Council and Chairman of the Yesha Council, responded to the events in Qusra in which a group of Israelis reportedly attempted to take over a Palestinian Arab house.

item.title: Historic moment: 21 years later, first families reestablish their homes in Ganim
item.description: 'Today, we are bringing life back to Ganim,' Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan said at a ceremony marking the reestablishment of the community, 21 years after the Disengagement. 'Ganim will become a huge community-10 times its current size!'

item.title: AI pushes Israeli teachers to bring exams back into the classroom
item.description: A new study finds Israeli teachers are increasingly moving assessments into the classroom as they grapple with concerns that AI could replace the skills students are meant to develop.

item.title: Tal Dardik returns to Temple Mount after release from detention
item.description: Welcomed by singing worshippers, Tal Dardik returned to the Temple Mount after his release from detention and received blessings for himself, his wife, and their newborn son.

item.title: Bank of Jerusalem CEO to employees: No connection between Mali Yahalomi's disappearance and the bank
item.description:
CEO of the Bank of Jerusalem, Yair Kaplan, where Mali worked, addressed employees in a letter regarding her disappearance. According to him, "Other than the fact that she is a bank employee, no connection has been found between the incident and the bank."
Kaplan emphasized that a gag order has been imposed on the incident and that it is forbidden to share information about the case.

item.title: Before the Word: Beethoven, the Shofar, and the Living Melody
item.description: The shofar does not teach what we never knew. It awakens what we have allowed ourselves to forget. Every generation sings the same nusach in prayer, yet no generation sings it in exactly the same way. It becomes a living thing.

item.title: IDF troops operating in southern Gaza yesterday identified a terrorist who crossed the Yellow Line
item.description:
IDF: Yesterday (Wednesday), IDF troops operating in the southern Gaza Strip identified a terrorist who crossed the Yellow Line and approached the troops in a manner that posed an immediate threat to them.
Following the identification, the troops responded with fire in order to respond to the threat. A hit was identified.
IDF troops under the Southern Command remain deployed in the area in accordance with the agreement and will continue to operate to remove any immediate threat.

item.title: IDF:
item.description: Security forces dismantle illegal outposts overnight; 51st Battalion soldiers prepared for security mission in Judea and Samaria.

item.title: Psychological warfare by lecturers against Israeli students
item.description: The Anti-Defamation League holds confidential briefing for students and staff, to expose how hatred toward Jews and Israelis has seeped into academic networks.

item.title: Police ask IDF to let arrested soldier continue training
item.description: Police reportedly asked the IDF to allow a soldier arrested over a shooting incident in Binyamin to continue his training while investigators await forensic evidence linking his weapon to the wounded child.

item.description: Calls received by MK Son Har-Melech indicate that candidates destined for service in combat units were informed only on their draft day that the ISA opposes their serving in the army.

item.title: A holy fire, a pure soul: William (Z'eev) Shakin, z"l
item.description: "Your heart was too big for this world."

item.title: Tradition or politics | Poll discloses what really irritates secular Israelis
item.description: 57% of secular Israelis support religious presence in the public realm, provided it is not forced. Two-thirds of young Israelis view Judaism in a positive light.

item.title: Theories about October 7th
item.description: Operational blindness or a deliberate strategic plan that went wrong? Will we ever know? Opinion.

item.title: October 7 survivors mark a full circle ahead of wedding
item.description: Ziv survived the Re'im shelter attack while Eliya spent 505 days in Gaza. Now, ahead of their wedding, a fellow victim's father will write their marriage contract.

item.title: Gush Etzion: Dozens of Palestinian Arabs riot, nine arrested
item.description: Judea and Samaria District Police arrest nine Palestinian Arabs after dozens attack Jews at Mikneh Avraham Farm.

item.title: Iranian President Pezeshkian meets incoming Basij commander
item.description:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met with Hossein Taeb, who was appointed commander of the Basij organization of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). During the meeting, Pezeshkian congratulated Taeb on his appointment.
Taeb, who previously served as head of the IRGC's Intelligence Organization and as commander of the Basij during the suppression of the 2009 protests, was appointed to the position by order of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, following the death of the previous commander, Gholam-Reza Soleimani.

item.title: Gag order imposed on investigation into disappearance of Mali and Liel Yahalomi.
item.description:
The family of Mali and Liel Yahalomi has pushed back against police briefings regarding their disappearance, saying there is no evidence to rule out a nationalistically motivated terror attack.
The family said they provided Lahav 433 investigators with all information in their possession and warned that some reports about the case contradict information they have received.
